newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally lower Tuesday amid early talk of steady cash prices, industry sources said.
May over-the-counter trade ranged from $1.94 to $1.95 after settling Monday at $1.953 per million British thermal units.
Early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., were talked unchanged at $1.97-2.02 per mmBtu as cooler-than-normal weather continued throughout most of the East and Midwest.
In ACCESS, May last traded 0.3 cent lower at $1.95.
Traders said support in May was at $1.88, and then at $1.85 and $1.825. Resistance was seen at $1.975, $1.99, $2.05 and $2.095.

In Monday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices were up slightly to the high-$1.90s. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-to-high $1.80s. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $2.40.
Early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 13 bcf of injections.
